title: Site web images: Apache replaces a child after 100 connections, so memory a heavy request grew is given back
steps: S1: From the checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap packages/fleet/tracy-fleet-operation/test/web-prefork-recycle.test.mjs
S2: Record the exit code and the result of the cases named in run.tests.
expect: web/tracy-prefork.conf sets a finite MaxConnectionsPerChild inside an mpm_prefork_module block, and both joomla.Dockerfile and wordpress.Dockerfile copy it into conf-enabled under a name that sorts before the demo limits file.
web/build.sh hashes tracy-prefork.conf for the joomla and wordpress images only; the demos and emdash hashes do not take it.
evidence: 16/11/2026 dev host: a customer Joomla site's web container held 550 MiB with 11 Apache children alive for 20 days, three at about 180 MB RSS, for 168 requests in 24 h; apache2ctl showed MaxConnectionsPerChild 0 (image default).
fence: Static checks of the conf, the Dockerfiles and build.sh; building the real images and moving a site on a host are not part of this case's run.

tests: the customer-site prefork file sets a finite MaxConnectionsPerChild
joomla.Dockerfile ships it into conf-enabled, ahead of the demo file
wordpress.Dockerfile ships it into conf-enabled, ahead of the demo file
only the joomla and wordpress image hashes take tracy-prefork.conf; demos and emdash do not
